title: The gharial's last stronghold

scenes.headline: Fewer than 1,000 adult gharials are left.

scenes.label: adult gharials in the wild (range 300–900)
scenes.body: Critically Endangered on the IUCN Red List (2019).
scenes.source: IUCN Red List, Lang et al. 2019

scenes.headline: live along one river: the Chambal
scenes.body: Most adults are inside India's National Chambal Sanctuary.

scenes.headline: A snout made for fish
scenes.body: Adults eat mainly fish, so they need clean, fish-rich rivers with sandbanks.

scenes.headline: Threats: sand mining, dams, nets
scenes.body: Losing sandbanks, river flow and fish pushes gharials out.

caption:
One river holds most of the world's gharials.

Smithsonian scientists report the population fell by 58% between 1997 and 2006.

Source: IUCN Red List (Lang, Chowfin & Ross 2019); Smithsonian's National Zoo; IUCN Crocodile Specialist Group. Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
notes: Conservation story anchored on a named place (National Chambal Sanctuary) and IUCN status with year. Media thin: only one wild gharial photo in the catalog, reused with different crops.
